pliosaurus:enwiki:6.title: Pliosaurus (Later discoveries and other species, part 3)

facts.statement: Pliosaurus fossils range from the Late Jurassic to the Lower Cretaceous, specifically from the Kimmeridgian to the Valanginian stages, with a possible record from the Oxfordian.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Jurassic to Lower Cretaceous (Kimmeridgian to Valanginian), Possible Oxfordian record

facts.statement: Although mentioned in 1824, Pliosaurus was not formally described until 1841 by Richard Owen, who first placed it in Plesiosaurus and later established it as its own genus.
facts.quote: Although initially mentioned in a 1824 paper by William Daniel Conybeare, it was not until 1841 that it was first formally described by Richard Owen as belonging to a new species of Plesiosaurus, before being given its own genus by the same author later that year.

facts.statement: The name Pliosaurus means "more lizard" because the animal's appearance was considered more reminiscent of crocodilians than of Plesiosaurus.
facts.quote: The genus name Pliosaurus means "more lizard", Owen naming the taxon of because its appearance being more reminiscent of crocodilians than to Plesiosaurus.

facts.statement: The largest species, P. funkei and P. kevani, are estimated to reach around 10 meters in length and weigh nearly 11 tonnes.
facts.quote: The largest species, P. funkei and P. kevani, are among the largest pliosaurs ever discovered, with maximum sizes estimated at around 10 m long and weighing nearly 11 t.

facts.statement: The skulls of the largest known Pliosaurus species exceed 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: The elongated skull of Pliosaurus is robust, and those of the largest known species exceed 2 m in length.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus teeth are robust and have a trihedral cross-section, which is a main diagnostic trait of the genus.
facts.quote: The teeth are also robust and are trihedral in cross-section, which is one of the main diagnostic traits of the genus.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus has a relatively short neck with only 18 cervical vertebrae compared to other plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: The neck is one of the most recognizable features of the taxon, being relatively short compared to other plesiosaurs, having only 18 cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus used its long, robust snouts to capture large prey by piercing them with numerous trihedral teeth located at the back of the jaws.
facts.quote: The long, robust snouts of the various Pliosaurus species were used to capture large prey, piercing them with the numerous trihedral teeth at the back of the jaws.

facts.statement: In 1841, Richard Owen described the Market Rasen specimen as the holotype of a new species, Plesiosaurus (Pleiosaurus) brachydeirus.
facts.quote: In 1841, Richard Owen described the anatomy of the jaws of the Market Rasen specimen. Based on several distinctive features, he decided to make it the holotype of a subgenus accompanying a new species of Plesiosaurus, which he named Plesiosaurus (Pleiosaurus) brachydeirus.

facts.statement: The specific name brachydeirus refers to the short cervical vertebrae of the specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name brachydeirus also comes from Ancient Greek and comes from the words βραχύς (brakhús, "short"), and δειρή (deirḗ, "neck" or "throat"), in reference to its cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: In 1871, John Phillips recognized P. brachydeirus as the type species and used the original spelling Pleiosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1871, John Phillips corrected most of Owen's taxonomic errors, recognizing P. brachydeirus as the type species and using the original spelling Pleiosaurus.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic classifications place Pliosaurus in a derived position within the Thalassophonea, often related to Gallardosaurus.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic classifications place Pliosaurus in a relatively derived position within the Thalassophonea, with the genus often being recovered as related to Gallardosaurus.

facts.statement: Since a 2013 paper, only six species have been firmly recognized as valid within the genus Pliosaurus.
facts.quote: While many species have been assigned to Pliosaurus in the past, only six are firmly recognised as valid since a 2013 paper.

facts.statement: Two additional species from Argentina named in 2014 and 2018 have not been fully confirmed as belonging to the genus in subsequent classifications.
facts.quote: Two additional species from Argentina were named in 2014 and 2018, but their assignment to the genus has not been fully confirmed in subsequent classifications.

facts.statement: In 1869, Richard Owen erroneously claimed that P. grandis was the type species of the genus.
facts.quote: In 1869, the same author erroneously claimed that another species formerly attributed to Pliosaurus, P. grandis, would be the type species of this genus.

facts.statement: Nestor Novozhilov named the species P. rossicus in 1948 based on partial specimens found in mines in the Lower Volga Basin, Russia.
facts.quote: In 1948, Nestor Novozhilov named the species P. rossicus on the basis of two more or less partial specimens discovered in two mines in the Lower Volga Basin in Russia

facts.statement: A more imposing specimen of P. rossicus, catalogued as PIN 2440/1, was discovered as a complete skeleton in May 1945.
facts.quote: The second specimen, more imposing and since catalogued as PIN 2440/1, was discovered in May 1945 as a complete skeleton

facts.statement: Fossils of P. funkei were collected at 2 km intervals during eight seasons of fieldwork from 2004 to 2012 by Jørn Hurum in the southern Sassenfjorden.
facts.quote: The fossils were collected at 2 km (1.25 mi) intervals during eight seasons of fieldwork conducted from 2004 to 2012 by Jørn Hurum in the southern Sassenfjorden

facts.statement: Based on morphological and histological characteristics like increased bone density, the two specimens of P. funkei appear to have been adults.
facts.quote: Based on various morphological and histological characteristics, particularly in terms of increased bone density, these two specimens appear to have been adults

facts.statement: Knutsen and colleagues suggest that P. funkei and P. rossicus might represent different growth stages of the same species, though they maintain them as distinct taxa.
facts.quote: In their article, Knutsen and colleagues conclude that it cannot be definitively excluded that P. funkei and P. rossicus would represent different ontogenetic stages of the same species based on the available material

facts.statement: The specific name P. funkei honors Bjørn Funke and his wife May-Liss Knudsen Funke for their voluntary service to the University of Oslo Natural History Museum.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Bjørn Funke, the discoverer of the holotype, and his wife May-Liss Knudsen Funke, for their years of voluntary service to the paleontological collections of the University of Oslo Natural History Museum

facts.statement: The species P. westburyensis and P. carpenteri were described in 2013, with holotypes discovered in a quarry near Westbury, Wiltshire.
facts.quote: The other two species described in the 2013 paper are P. westburyensis and P. carpenteri, both of whose holotypes were discovered in a quarry near Westbury, Wiltshire

facts.statement: The holotype of P. westburyensis (a skull with postcranial remains) was discovered on July 2, 1980, and the holotype of P. carpenteri (a partial skeleton) was discovered on May 12, 1994.
facts.quote: The holotype of the first species consists of a skull with some postcranial remains, while the second consists of a partial skeleton, respectively discovered on July 2, 1980, and May 12, 1994

facts.statement: Benson and colleagues argue that morphological differences between two Westbury specimens justify classifying them as separate species rather than intraspecific variation.
facts.quote: However, in the article published the following year, Benson and his colleagues consider that the differences between them are relatively significant when observed in the context of specimens from other localities, and therefore justify a specific distinction

facts.statement: The specific name P. westburyensis refers to the town of Westbury, while P. carpenteri honors Simon Carpenter, the discoverer of its holotype.
facts.quote: The specific name of the first cited species refers to the town of Westbury, while that of the second honours Simon Carpenter, discoverer of the holotype of the latter species

facts.statement: The species P. patagonicus was described in 2014 and P. almanzaensis in 2018 from fossils found in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: The South American species P. patagonicus and P. almanzaensis were described in 2014 and 2018, respectively, from fossils discovered in different localities of Neuquén Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype of P. patagonicus is a partial skull discovered in 1975 by Zulma Gasparini and a team from the La Plata Museum in the Zapala Department.
facts.quote: The holotype of P. patagonicus consists of a partial skull discovered in 1975 by Zulma Gasparini and a team from the La Plata Museum, in the Zapala Department.

facts.statement: The holotype of P. almanzaensis was discovered in 1986 by brothers Sergio and Rafael Cocca in Cajón de Almanza, about 10 km east of Loncopué.
facts.quote: It was discovered in 1986 by brothers Sergio and Rafael Cocca in the locality of Cajón de Almanza (hence the name), about 10 km east of the village of Loncopué.

facts.statement: P. almanzaensis was formally described in 2018 by O'Gorman, Gasparini, and Spalletti as a species living at the same time as P. patagonicus.
facts.quote: However, the specimen was only formally described in 2018 by O'Gorman, Gasparini, and Spalletti as representing a new species of Pliosaurus, contemporaneous with P. patagonicus.

facts.statement: A 2026 study estimated the body length of P. cf. kevani and P. funkei at 9.8 meters and their mass at approximately 10.7 to 10.9 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2026, Ruizhe Jackevan Zhao compared the specimens attributed to P. cf. kevani and P. funkei, and concluded that both would not be significantly different in terms of measurements, with an estimated body length of 9.8 m and body mass of approximately 10.7 – 10.9 t.

facts.statement: P. kevani is the only recognized species with sub-trihedral teeth that have slightly flattened labial surfaces and finely distributed enamel ridges.
facts.quote: However, P. kevani is the only recognized species in which the teeth are sub-trihedral in shape, possessing slightly flattened labial surfaces with finely distributed enamel ridges.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus was poorly understood for nearly two centuries because the holotype of P. brachydeirus lacked an adequate description.
facts.quote: Although being the type genus of pliosaurids, Pliosaurus was for nearly two centuries a poorly understood taxon due to the lack of an adequate description of the holotype of P. brachydeirus.

facts.statement: Halstead (then Tarlo) made the first revision of the Pliosaurus genus in 1960.
facts.quote: In 1960, Halstead (then called Tarlo) revised the taxonomy of Late Jurassic pliosaurids, making the first revision of the type genus.

facts.statement: An article by Knutsen concerning the taxonomic revision of Pliosaurus was published in 2012 alongside the official description of P. funkei.
facts.quote: Simultaneously with the publication of the official description of P. funkei in 2012, Another article written by Knutsen alone and concerning the taxonomic revision of the genus Pliosaurus as a whole is published.

facts.statement: Benson and colleagues recognized six valid Pliosaurus species in 2013.
facts.quote: In 2013, Benson and colleagues recognised the validity of the following six species: P. brachydeirus, P. rossicus, P. funkei, P. kevani, P. westburyensis, and P. carpenteri.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley named the family Pliosauridae in 1874 to include forms similar to Pliosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1874, Harry Govier Seeley named a new family of plesiosaurs, Pliosauridae, to contain forms similar to Pliosaurus.

facts.statement: Benson and colleagues found in 2012 that Pliosauridae is more closely related to Plesiosauroidea than to Rhomaleosauridae.
facts.quote: However, in 2012, Benson and colleagues recovered a different topology, with Pliosauridae being more closely related to Plesiosauroidea than Rhomaleosauridae.

facts.statement: Benson and Druckenmiller named the clade Thalassophonea within Pliosauridae in 2013.
facts.quote: In 2013, Benson and Druckenmiller named a new clade within Pliosauridae, Thalassophonea.

facts.statement: Fischer and colleagues placed P. patagonicus among the Cretaceous Brachaucheninae in 2023, while recovering P. almanzaensis within the genus Pliosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2023, Valentin Fischer and colleagues recovered P. almanzaensis within the genus in their cladograms, but placed P. patagonicus among the Brachaucheninae, a subgroup of thalassophoneans whose representatives mainly lived during the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus fossils range from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian).
facts.quote: fossil_range: Jurásico Superior (Kimmeridgiense)

facts.statement: The genus Pliosaurus was established by Owen in 1841.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Owen, 1841

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Pliosaurus is P. brachydeirus.
facts.quote: type_species: Pliosaurus brachydeirus

facts.statement: Multiple species have been assigned to Pliosaurus, including P. brachydeirus, P. carpenteri, P. funkei, P. macromerus, P. kevani, P. patagonicus, P. portentificus, P. rossicus, and P. westburyensis.
facts.quote: subdivision: P. brachydeirus Owen, 1840 P. carpenteri Benson et al., 2013 P. funkei Knutsen, Druckenmiller & Hurum, 2012 P. macromerus Philips, 1871 P. kevani Benson et al., 2013 P. patagonicus Gasparini & O'Gorman, 2014 P. portentificus Noè et al., 2004 P. rossicus Novozhilov, 1948 P. westburyensis Benson et al., 2013

facts.statement: Knutsen maintains the validity of P. brachyspondylus and P. macromerus based on proposed neotypes, though their original types are non-diagnostic.
facts.quote: However, he maintains the validity of both species P. brachyspondylus and P. macromerus on the basis of proposed neotypes, their original type specimens being deemed non-diagnostic.

facts.statement: P. andrewsi is no longer considered a valid species of Pliosaurus due to having too many morphological differences.
facts.quote: P. andrewsi, which was long considered a valid species of the genus, turns out to have too many morphological differences to be placed in Pliosaurus.

facts.statement: The exact relationship of pliosaurids to other plesiosaurs remains uncertain.
facts.quote: Exactly how pliosaurids are related to other plesiosaurs is uncertain.

facts.statement: Smith and Dyke considered Pliosaurus to be the sister taxon of Peloneustes in 2008.
facts.quote: In 2008, Adam S. Smith and Gareth J. Dyke considered Pliosaurus to be the sister taxon of Peloneustes.

facts.statement: Páramo-Fonseca and colleagues argued in 2019 that P. patagonicus and P. almanzaensis do not form a monophyletic group with European Pliosaurus species.
facts.quote: In 2019, María Páramo-Fonseca and colleagues considered that these two taxa do not appear to form a monophyletic group with the European species of the genus.

facts.statement: Alternative cladograms by Fischer et al. sometimes recover P. patagonicus as the sister taxon of the Russian genus Luskhan.
facts.quote: Some of their alternative cladograms even recover the species as the sister taxon of the Russian genus Luskhan.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus is an extinct genus of saurischian reptiles belonging to the suborder Pliosauroidea.
facts.quote: Pliosaurus (del griego "más cercano al lagarto"), o pliosaurio, es un género extinto de reptiles saurópsidos del suborden de los pliosauroides

facts.statement: Pliosaurus were giant predators that fed on fish, squid, and other marine reptiles.
facts.quote: Eran gigantescos depredadores, que se alimentaban a base de peces, calamares, y otros reptiles marinos

facts.statement: Unlike other pliosaurids, Pliosaurus had teeth that were triangular in cross-section.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros pliosáuridos, Pliosaurus tenía dientes de aspecto triangular en corte transversal

facts.statement: Richard Owen described the type specimen of Pliosaurus brachydeirus.
facts.quote: cuando Richard Owen describió el espécimen tipo de Pliosaurus brachydeirus

facts.statement: Owen previously used a similar name, Pleiosaurus, as a subgenus of Plesiosaurus for plesiosaurs with shortened vertebrae.
facts.quote: el mismo Owen había usado un nombre similar como subgénero de Plesiosaurus, Pleiosaurus, para los plesiosaurios con las vértebras acortadas

facts.statement: Owen described the genus Pliosaurus in 1841.
facts.quote: Owen, al describir el género en 1841

facts.statement: Owen described the species Pliosaurus brachyspondylus in 1839.
facts.quote: Owen describió a esta especie en 1839

facts.statement: Pliosaurus rossicus is a relatively small pliosaur known from two specimens discovered in Chuvashia, Russia.
facts.quote: Pliosaurus rossicus es un pliosaurio relativamente pequeño conocido a partir de dos especímenes descubiertos en Chuvashia, Rusia

facts.statement: Pliosaurus rossicus was described as a species of Pliosaurus in 1948.
facts.quote: Esta especie fue descrita en 1948 como una especie de Pliosaurus

facts.statement: In March 2009, the Natural History Museum of Oslo announced the discovery of a fossil possibly belonging to the genus Pliosaurus.
facts.quote: En marzo de 2009 el Museo de Historia Natural de Oslo anunció el descubrimiento del fósil de una criatura posiblemente perteneciente al género Pliosaurus

facts.statement: The remains of the creature, which lived about 147 million years ago, are exhibited at the Natural History Museum of Oslo.
facts.quote: Los restos de la criatura, que vivió hace unos 147 millones de años, son exhibidos en el Museo de Historia Natural de Oslo

facts.statement: The predator's remains were discovered in permafrost in Svalbard, Norway, in June 2006.
facts.quote: Los restos del depredador fueron descubiertos en el permafrost en Svalbard, Noruega, en junio de 2006

facts.statement: The remains were finally excavated in mid-2008 during the boreal summer by a Norwegian team led by Jørn Hurum.
facts.quote: y finalmente excavados a mediados de 2008, durante el verano boreal, por un equipo noruego liderado por Jørn Hurum

facts.statement: Pliosaurus belongs to the suborder Pliosauroidea.
facts.quote: del suborden de los pliosauroides

facts.statement: The parent group of Pliosaurus is Thalassophonea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Thalassophonea

facts.statement: Pliosaurus belongs to the family Pliosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Pliosauridae

facts.statement: Pliosaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Pliosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic in what is now Europe and South America.
facts.quote: que vivieron durante el Jurásico Superior, en lo que hoy es Europa y América del Sur

facts.statement: Pliosaurus portentificus originates from the late Kimmeridgian of England.
facts.quote: Pliosaurus portentificus procede de finales del Kimmeridgiense de Inglaterra

facts.statement: Due to the distribution pattern of pliosaurians, it is believed they had a cosmopolitan distribution, similar to modern whales.
facts.quote: Debido al patrón de distribución de los pliosaurios se cree que tenían distribución cosmopolita, como las ballenas actuales

facts.statement: The time range for Pliosaurus is from the Callovian to the Maastrichtian (165.3 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Maastrichtian (165.3 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Re-examination of the Svalbard specimen fossils revised the estimated total length to a range of 10.0 to 12.8 meters.
facts.quote: El escrutinio de los fósiles del espécimen de Svalbard reveló que no era tan grande como se afirmó en un principio; la longitud total estimada se ha revisado llegando a un rango de 10.0 - 12.8 metros

facts.statement: Analysis of the four flipper bones suggests the animal swam using only its two front flippers, using the rear pair only for extra thrust when chasing and capturing prey.
facts.quote: Análisis de los huesos de las cuatro aletas sugieren que el animal nadaba usando solo sus dos aletas anteriores, usando el par posterior solo cuando necesitaba un empuje adicional para perseguir y capturar a sus presas

facts.statement: The assignment of Pliosaurus macromerus to the genus Pliosaurus is unclear.
facts.quote: su pertenencia al género Pliosaurus no es clara

facts.statement: According to Knutsen (2012), there is no reason to classify Pliosaurus andrewsi within the genus Pliosaurus.
facts.quote: según Knutsen (2012) no hay razón para clasificarlo dentro del género Pliosaurus

facts.statement: Knutsen (2012) provisionally retained Pliosaurus rossicus as a separate species but noted that further examination is needed to determine if it is a distinct taxon or merely a modern synonym of Pliosaurus macromerus.
facts.quote: Knutsen (2012) lo retuvo provisionalmente como una especie separada, pero subrayó que se necesitan exámenes adicionales para determinar si P. rossicus es ciertamente un taxón separado o meramente un sinónimo más moderno de Pliosaurus macromerus

facts.statement: Knutsen (2012) considers Pliosaurus portentificus a nomen dubium because its holotype specimen likely belongs to a juvenile individual of another Pliosaurus species.
facts.quote: Es considerado por Knutsen (2012) como un nomen dubium, dado que su espécimen holotipo muy probablemente pertenece a un individuo juvenil de alguna de las otras especies de Pliosaurus
